text:
sasha: Hey — seeing a p95 spike on the AMD serving pool for short sequences (seq <= 32). Perf bot raised a regression after last night's roll. Logs show a fallback to generic_matmul due to no optimized kernel match for gfx90a + int8 + short seq. Anybody seen this?

perf-bot: perf-alert: cluster=amd-prod-2 metric=p95_token_latency change=+42% window=22:00-22:30 UTC sample_log:
[ERROR] kernel_lookup: no candidate for (arch=gfx90a, dtype=int8, seq=16) -> falling back to generic_matmul

anil: Is this the quant-int8 opset we onboarded on Thurs? I remember the build for gfx90a was flaky. I'll check the kernel registry + build logs.

megan: We rolled canary "quant-int8-v2" at 17:30 UTC and reverted at 18:05. The regression surfaced in stable traffic too (some routes still hit canary traffic).

sasha: Noticed KV cache hit rate dropped ~15% in the same window — might be related. Also batcher metrics show avg_batch_size went 1.8 -> 1.2, so fewer coalesced requests. If the fast kernel is missing, per-token compute is slower and batching TTLs time out more often.

anil: Quick check: querying kernel registry now:
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KREG_TOKEN" \"https://kernel-registry.internal/api/kernels?arch=gfx90a&dtype=int8&opset=quant-int8-v2\"
```
sample response: `[]` (no builds found for that combo)

megan: Oof. That matches. Two immediate mitigations: 1) add a conditional route to divert gfx90a short-seq traffic to the older int8-compatible pool that has a working kernel, or 2) increase batch_timeout_ms so batching has more time to accumulate (trade higher tail latency but fewer fallbacks). Thoughts?

sasha: Prefer option 1 for now — lower blast radius. Proposed routing patch (policy snippet):
```yaml
- name: amd-shortseq-fallback
  when:
    - kernel_lookup: no_candidate
    - request.arch: gfx90a
    - request.sequence_length: <=32
  then:
    - route: amd-generic-int8-pool
    - override: prefer_fastpath=false
    - adjust: batch_timeout_ms: +10
```

megan: I can apply a temporary route. Another idea: try conditional variant probe before full fallback — attempt to match older opset (quant-int8-v1) or f16-compatible kernel. That might be faster than generic_matmul.

asaha: (typo) sorry

sasha: +1 to probing older opset first. Example check-flow: try kernel_lookup(opset=v2) -> if empty try kernel_lookup(opset=v1,dtype=float16) -> if empty fallback pool. This preserves better perf in many cases.

anil: I'll add logging to kernel-discovery to emit the candidate list & reason_code so we can track missing patterns. Also kicking off a build for gfx90a-int8-opset-v2 now (queued). ETA ~6 hours for a green artifact depending on CI.

megan: Applying routing rule to amd-prod-2 now, will tail logs and dashboards. :eyes:

perf-bot: update: after route applied at 22:05 UTC on amd-prod-2, p95_token_latency decreased ~12% vs the spike. Monitoring: p95 still ~8% above baseline across other regions.

sasha: Great. Can we also run a small synthetic eval to confirm KV cache interplay? Plan: force many seq=16 requests with identical prefixes and measure: latency, batch_size, kv_hit_rate. I'll post the eval script.

anil: Logged: KERNEL_DISCOVERY_PROBE entries added. Will attach build URL once CI finishes.

megan: Monitoring update in ~15m. If stable, will keep route for 24h and then remove once kernel build is verified.

sasha: Thanks all. Follow-ups: anil -> post kernel build link + reason codes; megan -> keep the route and dashboard alerts; I'll create the eval and share results here.

megan: applied. alerting: @channel if p95 > baseline+20% for 10m.

perf-bot: note: regression ticket #INF-3142 created for tracking (linked to kernel-build task).
